1 # Variables and Expressions 2 3 Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files. 4 5 > **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow. 6 > 7 > `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors: 8 > 9 > - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107) 10 > - Invented `nodes..output` syntax 11 > - References to unknown variables or node IDs 12 > - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false` 13 > 14 > Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## Table of contents 19 20 - [Variables Overview](#variables-overview) 21 - [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals) 22 - [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes) 23 - [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates) 24 - [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes) 25 - [Expression System](#expression-system) 26 - [Available Globals](#available-globals) 27 - [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts) 28 - [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints) 29 - [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules) 30 - [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli) 31 - [Complete Example](#complete-example) 32 33 --- 34 35 ## Variables Overview 36 37 Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 --- 542 543 ## Scoping Rules 544 545 ### Node Output Availability 546 547 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 560 561 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 562 563 ### Subflow Scope 564 565 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 566 567 --- 568 569 ## Variable Management via CLI 570 571 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 572 573 ### Adding a workflow input variable 574 575 1. Open `.flow` 576 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 577 3. 1	# Activities
2	
3	Activities are pre-built actions available for each connector (e.g., "Send Message", "Create Issue"). They represent specific operations the connector supports. Activities include both **actions** (non-trigger) and **triggers** (event listeners).
4	
5	> Full command syntax and options: [uip-commands.md — Integration Service](../uip-commands.md#integration-service-is). Domain-specific usage patterns are shown inline below.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## List Activities (Non-Trigger)
10	
11	Use the connector **Key**, not the display name. For Salesforce, the canonical key is `uipath-salesforce-sfdc`; do not pass `salesforce` or `uipath-salesforce` to activity commands.
12	
13	```bash
14	uip is activities list "<connector-key>" --output json
15	```
16	
17	```bash
18	uip is activities list "uipath-salesforce-sfdc" --output json
19	```
20	
21	This lists **non-trigger activities only** (actions, not event listeners).
22	
23	## List Trigger Activities
24	
25	```bash
26	uip is activities list "<connector-key>" --triggers --output json
27	```
28	
29	```bash
30	uip is activities list "uipath-salesforce-sfdc" --triggers --output json
31	```
32	
33	The `--triggers` flag filters to **trigger activities only** (`isTrigger=true`). These represent events the connector can fire (e.g., "Record Created", "Record Updated").
34	
35	The **Operation** field on trigger activities indicates the trigger type:
36	- **CREATED** / **UPDATED** / **DELETED** — CRUD event triggers (require an intermediate "objects" step to discover which objects support the operation)
37	- Other values — custom event triggers (skip directly to metadata)
38	
39	> When a trigger activity is selected, proceed to [triggers.md](triggers.md) for the trigger metadata workflow.
40	
41	## Response Fields
42	
43	| Field | Description |
44	|---|---|
45	| **`Name`** | Activity identifier |
46	| `DisplayName` | Human-readable name (e.g., "HTTP Request", "Send Message") |
47	| `Description` | What the activity does |
48	| **`ObjectName`** | The resource object this activity operates on (use as `<object-name>` in trigger describe for non-CRUD triggers) |
49	| `MethodName` | HTTP method used (GET, POST, etc.) |
50	| **`Operation`** | Operation type — for triggers, this is the event type (CREATED, UPDATED, DELETED, or custom) |
51	| `IsCurated` | Whether this is a curated/recommended activity |
52	
53	---
54	
55	## When to Use Activities vs Resources vs Triggers
56	
57	- **Activities** = named actions (e.g., "Send Email"). Discovered via `is activities list`.
58	- **Triggers** = event listeners (e.g., "Record Created"). Discovered via `is activities list --triggers`. Metadata via `is triggers objects` / `is triggers describe`. See [triggers.md](triggers.md).
59	- **Resources** = data objects with CRUD (e.g., "Account"). Discovered via `is resources list`. Executed via `is resources run <verb>`.
60	
61	> After listing activities, present the available actions to the user. Activities provide context for what a connector can do — use this to guide which resource operations, triggers, or workflow actions to pursue.
62	
63	---
64	
65	## Filter Trees (CEQL)
66	
67	Some IS activities — most notably **List All Records** and other list/query operations — accept a server-side filter expressed in **CEQL** (Connector Expression Query Language). As with trigger filters (which compile to JMESPath), CEQL filters are authored as a **structured filter tree** and the CLI compiles them to a CEQL string. Authoring as a tree keeps the CLI and Studio Web in lockstep so the activity round-trips cleanly when re-opened in SW.
68	
69	### Contract — three signals from IS metadata
70	
71	The CLI reads the live IS metadata response and uses three signals to wire the filter:
72	
73	1. **The activity supports CEQL** when one of its `parameters` declares `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. That parameter's `name` is the connector-specific key the compiled CEQL string is sent under — most commonly `where`, but **not always** (e.g. Salesforce uses `q`). Activities with no such parameter do not support server-side filtering — pass no `filter` and filter downstream.
74	2. **A field is filterable** when its IS metadata entry has `searchable: true`. Type alone does not gate it — the connector flags fields explicitly. Fields without `searchable: true` are rejected by the CLI even if they look like primitives.
75	3. **Permitted operators** for the field are listed under `searchableOperators`. **Connector-side identifier** for the field in CEQL is `searchableNames[0]` when present (some connectors expose a friendly `name` but require a different identifier in the query string).
76	
77	### What the CLI persists from a single `filter` input
78	
79	- **Runtime side** — the compiled CEQL string lands at `inputs.detail.queryParameters.<filterParamName>` where `<filterParamName>` is the FilterBuilder parameter's name from the IS metadata (often `where`).
80	- **Design-time side** — the structured tree is embedded under `inputs.detail.configuration`'s `essentialConfiguration.savedFilterTrees.<filterParamName>`. Studio Web reads this on open to re-render the filter widget; without it the filter UI shows up empty even though the runtime call still works.
81	
82	Pass `filter` (the structured tree) and the CLI emits both halves in lockstep. Passing both `filter` and `queryParameters.<filterParamName>` is rejected at validation time — single source of truth.
83	
84	### Tree shape
85	
86	Identical to the trigger filter tree — the same `FilterTree` / `Filter` / `WorkflowValue` types are used; only the compiler output (CEQL vs JMESPath) differs.
87	
88	```jsonc
89	{
90	  "groupOperator": 0,             // 0 = And, 1 = Or — combines sibling filters/groups
91	  "index": 0,                     // ordering index within parent (root is 0)
92	  "filters": [                    // leaf conditions at this level
93	    {
94	      "id": "<fieldName>",        // resource field name from `is resources describe`
95	      "operator": "<Operator>",   // PascalCase, see operator table below
96	      "value": {
97	        "value": <typed value>,   // string / number / boolean / ISO-8601 date-time / array
98	        "rawString": "\"...\"",   // verbatim user-entered text (with quotes for strings)
99	        "isLiteral": true         // literals only — expression values are not yet supported
100	      }
101	    }
102	  ],
103	  "groups": []                    // optional: nested subgroups (same shape as root)
104	}
105	```
106	
107	A no-op filter — used when the user wants to list all records without restriction — is `null` or `{"groupOperator": null, "index": 0, "filters": []}`. Prefer **omitting** the `filter` field entirely.
108	
109	### Compiled CEQL output
110	
111	The CLI compiles each leaf to `<field> <op> <value>` (or `<field> <function>` for null checks) and joins siblings with the group operator. String values are wrapped in single quotes; booleans, numerics, and enums are passed bare.
112	
113	| Operator | CEQL token | Notes |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| `Equals` | `=` | |
116	| `NotEquals` | `!=` | |
117	| `LessThan` / `LessThanOrEqual` / `GreaterThan` / `GreaterThanOrEqual` | `<` / `<=` / `>` / `>=` | Numeric / date-time |
118	| `Contains` / `NotContains` | `Contains` / `Not Contains` | Substring (string) |
119	| `StartsWith` / `NotStartsWith` / `EndsWith` / `NotEndsWith` | `Starts With` / `Not Starts With` / `Ends With` / `Not Ends With` | String |
120	| `Like` / `NotLike` | `Like` / `Not Like` | Pattern match (connector-specific) |
121	| `In` / `NotIn` | `In` / `Not In` | Membership — `value.value` is a list; rendered as `(v1, v2, …)` |
122	| `IsNull` / `IsNotNull` | `Is Null` / `Is Not Null` | No `value` needed |
123	| `Is` / `IsNot` | `=` against literal `true` / `false` | Boolean shortcut |
124	
125	Logical operators between siblings:
126	
127	| `groupOperator` | CEQL token |
128	|---|---|
129	| `0` (And) | ` AND ` |
130	| `1` (Or) | ` OR ` |
131	
132	### Examples
133	
134	**Active accounts only:**
135	
136	```json
137	{
138	  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
139	  "filters": [
140	    { "id": "Status", "operator": "Equals",
141	      "value": { "value": "Active", "rawString": "\"Active\"", "isLiteral": true } }
142	  ]
143	}
144	```
145	→ CEQL: `Status = 'Active'`
146	
147	**Score ≥ 80 AND Region in (EMEA, APAC):**
148	
149	```json
150	{
151	  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
152	  "filters": [
153	    { "id": "Score", "operator": "GreaterThanOrEqual",
154	      "value": { "value": 80, "rawString": "80", "isLiteral": true } },
155	    { "id": "Region", "operator": "In",
156	      "value": { "value": ["EMEA", "APAC"], "rawString": "[\"EMEA\",\"APAC\"]", "isLiteral": true } }
157	  ]
158	}
159	```
160	→ CEQL: `Score >= 80 AND Region In ('EMEA', 'APAC')`
161	
162	**Subject contains "urgent" AND (owner = me OR owner is null):**
163	
164	```json
165	{
166	  "groupOperator": 0, "index": 0,
167	  "filters": [
168	    { "id": "Subject", "operator": "Contains",
169	      "value": { "value": "urgent", "rawString": "\"urgent\"", "isLiteral": true } }
170	  ],
171	  "groups": [
172	    {
173	      "groupOperator": 1, "index": 1,
174	      "filters": [
175	        { "id": "OwnerId", "operator": "Equals",
176	          "value": { "value": "${me.id}", "rawString": "\"${me.id}\"", "isLiteral": false } },
177	        { "id": "OwnerId", "operator": "IsNull" }
178	      ]
179	    }
180	  ]
181	}
182	```
183	→ CEQL: `Subject Contains 'urgent' AND (OwnerId = ${me.id} OR OwnerId Is Null)`. Non-literal values (`isLiteral: false`) are emitted as `${expression}` placeholders for runtime resolution.
184	
185	### How to build a CEQL filter tree
186	
187	1. Run `uip is resources describe "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" --connection-id "<id>" --operation List` to read the resource's metadata.
188	2. **Confirm CEQL is supported** for this operation: at least one entry under `parameters` must carry `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. If none does, the activity does not support server-side filtering — omit `filter` and filter downstream (e.g. with a Script node).
189	3. **Pick filterable fields** from `fields[]` where `searchable: true`. Other fields will be rejected by the CLI at configure time even if they look like primitives.
190	4. For each leaf, pick an operator from the field's `searchableOperators` list (when present). Date-time fields take ISO-8601 strings; enums take the literal enum value.
191	5. Use the field's `name` as the leaf `id`. The CLI rewrites it to `searchableNames[0]` when emitting CEQL if the connector declares one — you don't need to use the alias yourself.
192	6. Build one leaf per condition; place multiple conditions under the same `groupOperator` (0 for AND, 1 for OR). Use nested `groups` for mixed AND/OR.
193	7. Wrap values in a `WorkflowValue` object with `value`, `rawString`, `isLiteral`. Strings, numbers, booleans, dates, and arrays are all valid `value` types; only `isLiteral: true` is currently supported by activity-side compilation.
194	
195	### What NOT to generate
196	
197	| Invalid input | Why it fails | Valid replacement |
198	|---|---|---|
199	| `"filter": "Status = 'Active'"` | Bare CEQL string — `filter` must be an object. | Structured tree with `filters: [...]`. |
200	| `"filterExpression": "..."` | That field is reserved for the trigger (JMESPath) path. | Use `filter` (CEQL tree) for activities. |
201	| `{ "operator": "equals", ... }` | Operator is case-sensitive. | `"operator": "Equals"` |
202	| `{ "value": "Active" }` on a leaf | Bare string — must be wrapped in the `WorkflowValue` object. | `{ "value": { "value": "Active", "rawString": "\"Active\"", "isLiteral": true } }` |
203	| `{ "id": "fields.Status", ... }` | `fields.` prefix — use the bare field name from `is resources describe`. | `{ "id": "Status", ... }` |
204	| `{ "id": "<field without searchable: true>", ... }` | The CLI checks `searchable` on the IS metadata entry; non-searchable fields are rejected even if their type looks filterable. | Pick a field where `searchable: true`. |
205	| `"queryParameters": { "where": "..." }` alongside `filter` | Hardcoding `where` assumes that's the FilterBuilder param name — it isn't always (Salesforce uses `q`, etc.). | Pass `filter` only; the CLI discovers the right param name from `design.component === "FilterBuilder"`. |
206	| `In` operator with a single value not in a list | `In` expects an array `value`. | Use `Equals`, or pass `value: ["one"]`. |
207	
208	## Custom Fields (`objectActions[ActionType=Api]`)
209	
210	Connectors with extensible/custom fields (Jira project+issuetype → custom Jira fields, Mailchimp list_id → audience merge fields, Salesforce custom objects) expose `Api`-type entries under `objectActions[]`. Each entry's `apiConfiguration.url`/`body` carries `{token}` placeholders naming the parent fields. The runtime replays the ObjectAction with cached parent values to fetch the connector-specific custom-field schema.
211	
212	**For Maestro flows**, this lives on the activity node as `essentialConfiguration.customFieldsRequestDetails`. Authoring contract → [uipath-maestro-flow connector/impl.md Step 6c](../../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md).
213	
214	Shape:
215	
216	```json
217	"customFieldsRequestDetails": {
218	  "objectActionName": "GenerateSchema",
219	  "parameterValues": [["fields_sub_project_sub_key", "ENGCE"], ...]
220	}
221	```
222	
223	camelCase inner keys, `parameterValues` as `[key, value]` tuples (Studio Web emits `Map<string,string|null>` via `Array.from(entries())`). Object-map form rejected by the CLI.
224

**Summary**

**Topology:** `start` (manual trigger) fans out in parallel to `queryErpLineItems1` and `queryCrmAccount1` → both rejoin at `mergeBranches` (parallel gateway) → `computeOvercharge` (script) → `endSuccess`.

- **Trigger inputs:** `invoiceNumber`, `accountNumber` (string), `disputedLineNumber`, `disputedUnitPrice`, `disputedQuantity` (number) — all `in` globals bound to `start`.
- **`queryErpLineItems1`** — Data Fabric `Query Entity Records` on entity `BillingDisputeERP`, CEQL filter `invoiceNumber = '<invoiceNumber>'`.
- **`queryCrmAccount1`** — same connector on entity `BillingDisputeCRM`, CEQL filter `accountNumber = '<accountNumber>'`. (Both nodes share the tenant's single Data Fabric connection — `flow validate` flags this as an informational warning about shared-connection state, expected since only one connection exists.)
- **`computeOvercharge`** (script node): finds the ERP row matching `disputedLineNumber`, computes `invoiced = unitPrice * quantity`, `totalOvercharge = max(invoiced - contracted, 0)`, `discrepancyCount = 1|0`, `matchedInvoiceNumber` from the first ERP row, `accountTier` from the CRM row.
- **`endSuccess`** maps all four outputs (`totalOvercharge`, `discrepancyCount`, `matchedInvoiceNumber`, `accountTier`).

**Validation:** `uip maestro flow validate` → `Status: Valid` (one informational shared-connection warning, not a defect). `uip maestro flow format` applied successfully.

No mocks, no missing connections — both Data Fabric queries are live-configured against the actual `BillingDisputeERP`/`BillingDisputeCRM` entities and connection in this tenant, so it's ready for `flow debug`. Let me know if you'd like me to run debug, publish to Studio Web, or deploy.
